title: Sample 13-7: Prose Poem

blocks.features: Italic work-title, followed by the bracketed section title 'A Chair' in plain roman.

blocks.text: A widow in a wise veil and more garments shows that shadows are even. It addresses no more, it shadows the stage and learning. A regular arrangement, the severest and the most preserved is that which has the arrangement not more than always authorised.
blocks.features: First prose paragraph, ordinary indented paragraph format.

blocks.text: A suitable establishment, well housed, practical, patient and staring, a suitable bedding, very suitable and not more particularly than complaining, anything suitable is so necessary.
blocks.features: Second prose paragraph; print excerpt ends with an ellipsis, showing more text follows that is not included.
